limitations: required_capabilities lists coarse prerequisites for checking each obligation, including unmapped obligations, rather than exhaustive target implementation dependencies. Tags follow the cited public contracts and the stated observations. Fixture repository operations require local-repository; merely querying configuration does not require app execution. A runnable-content preservation assertion does require sandbox-execution even when its primary command is info or uninstall. installation permits any installation profile, while user-installation and system-installation select specific profiles. system-authorization covers authorized system changes or explicit privilege checks, not ordinary read-only system queries. Session services, fault injection and other specialized capabilities are included only where the obligation needs them; alternative fixture provisioning may have additional prerequisites.

This is a curated, source-backed behavior obligation catalogue, not all CLI behavior. Every active canonical command has at least one obligation, but neither command presence nor option presence means its behavior is fully covered. The complete mechanical command/option denominator is separate.

Granularity varies with the observable contract. Rows are not weighted by complexity, risk, or frequency, and a percentage over these rows measures only this catalogue. No test credits or execution results are assigned here.

Sources are repository public manpage documents. Anchors identify section titles, option text, or quoted prose after XML text normalization. app/flatpak-main.c was consulted only to identify active canonical command names; hidden deprecated aliases and the separate flatpak-spawn executable are outside this scope.

The command descriptions support lifecycle operations, but do not expressly specify the full error/recovery contracts retained at the user's request: cli.install.user.missing-ref, cli.info.user.absent-ref, cli.uninstall.user.absent-ref, cli.update.user.failed-download-preserves, cli.update.user.noop, and cli.update.user.retry. Their nonzero statuses, diagnostic identification, unchanged deployments, and successful retry/no-op expectations are compatibility obligations inferred from those operations, not verbatim documented guarantees. The docs do not prescribe the runner's accepted diagnostic strings or its payload request pattern.

cli.install.user.already-installed is grounded in the documented warning-and-ignore behavior under --or-update; an explicit zero exit status is not stated there. cli.install.user.runtime-dependency is supported by the dependency options and runtime-resolution documentation, rather than a detailed dependency transaction specification. Empty enumeration and unsuccessful absent-ref queries are consequences of the documented query domains, not specified output byte layouts.

User and system are selected installation profiles, not privilege levels. Session document/permission and running-instance commands are any because they do not select an installation; they still operate in a user's session. Build/repository commands are any when their result is independent of the installation providing prerequisites. Explicit system obligations require separate evidence and remain untested by the existing user-only scenarios.

Known omissions include exhaustive partial-ref/fuzzy-match and interactive choice cases, option ordering and repeated-option precedence, every output column and ellipsization mode, localization and terminal formatting, cancellation/crash/concurrency and disk-full recovery, and combinations across architectures, branches, remotes and installations.

Sandbox obligations sample filesystem, environment, network, bus and conditional permissions. They do not enumerate every socket, device, feature, USB query, namespace, nested sandbox, permission-layer interaction or parental-control policy. Document/permission obligations do not enumerate every portal-specific table schema or desktop integration.

Distribution obligations do not enumerate OCI transports/compression, authenticators, redirects, mirror selection, every signature failure mode, extra-data scripts, extension/subset rules, all static-delta strategies, or every vendor preinstall/configuration key. Build options are represented by selected output contracts, not one generated row per flag.

Manpage inconsistencies are not resolved through private code: run's --nousb term differs from its prose and build-finish's query syntax; the global Commands section omits active commands such as preinstall, which has its own manpage. Omitted disputed details should not be inferred as tested contracts. Version-specific features require evidence from a target that supports them.
